title_en: Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Branch v. Meizhou Mediterranean Hotel Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over loan contract
ruling_gist_en: Entrusted loans have been incorporated into the national financial regulatory framework, with financial institutions acting as lenders and performing corresponding duties. On the other hand, due to their funding sources and other characteristics, they share similarities with private lending, exhibiting features of both financial loans and private lending in different aspects. In the absence of explicit provisions in current laws and judicial interpretations, the applicable rules may be determined by analyzing whether entrusted loans are more akin to financial loans or private lending in their characteristics. Given that the main terms of an entrusted loan contract, such as the borrower, amount, term, and interest rate, are determined according to the entrusting party's will, and the entrusting party enjoys the main contractual rights, including the interest income from the loan, and considering that entrusted loans and private lending share the same source of funds, it can be inferred that their funding costs are roughly equivalent. Therefore, when a people's court determines the upper limit of the interest rate for an entrusted loan contract, it should refer to the relevant rules on private lending.

full_text_en:
Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Branch

v.

Meizhou Mediterranean Hotel Co., Ltd., et al.

— dispute over loan contract

【Ruling Summary】

An entrusted loan falls within the scope of national financial regulation, with a financial institution acting as the lender and performing corresponding duties. On the other hand, due to its characteristics such as the source of funds, it shares commonalities with private lending, reflecting features of both financial loans and private lending in different aspects. Where no clear provisions exist in current laws and judicial interpretations, the applicable rules may be determined by analyzing whether the entrusted loan is more similar to a financial loan or to private lending. Given that the principal terms of an entrusted loan contract, such as the borrower, loan amount, term, and interest rate, are determined according to the principal's instructions, and the principal enjoys the main rights under the contract, such as the interest income from the loan, and considering that the cost of funds for entrusted loans and private lending can be presumed to be roughly equivalent based on the same source of funds, the people's court shall, when determining the upper limit of the interest rate for an entrusted loan contract, refer to the relevant rules on private lending.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2018) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 54

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Meizhou Mediterranean Hotel Co., Ltd., domiciled at Wangjianglou, Jiangbian Road, Meizhou City, Guangdong Province.

Person in Charge: Liu Ling, Branch Manager.

Defendant at First Instance: Huang Hua, male, born on July 29, 1955, resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, currently residing at Tianhe Road, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Ding Jianqing, lawyer at Zhong Lun Law Firm (Guangzhou).

Agent ad litem: Zhang Zixiang, lawyer at Zhong Lun Law Firm (Guangzhou).

Defendant at First Instance: Wang Hui, male, born on February 14, 1983, Han nationality, residing at Baiyun District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Ding Jianqing, lawyer at Zhong Lun Law Firm (Guangzhou).

Agent ad litem: Zhang Zixiang, lawyer at Zhong Lun Law Firm (Guangzhou).

Defendant at First Instance: Li Qiong, female, born on September 5, 1973, Han nationality, residing at Luohu District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Ding Jianqing, lawyer at Zhong Lun Law Firm (Guangzhou).

Agent ad litem: Zhang Zixiang, lawyer at Zhong Lun Law Firm (Guangzhou).

Third Party at First Instance: Hou Chuxiong, male, born on December 18, 1957, Han nationality, residing at Jinping District, Shantou City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Ma Hao, lawyer at Guangdong Shenjinniu Law Firm.

The retrial applicant, Meizhou Mediterranean Hotel Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mediterranean Hotel) filed a petition for retrial with this Court against the civil judgment (hereinafter referred to as the original judgment) of the Guangdong High People's Court in the case of dispute over a loan contract with the respondent, Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Branch (hereinafter referred to as SPD Bank), the second instance appellants Shenzhen Zirui Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zirui Company), Sun Century Real Estate Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sun Century Company), and Meizhou Lizhen Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lizhen Company), and the defendants at first instance Huang Hua, Wang Hui, Li Qiong, and the third party at first instance Hou Chuxiong. On November 30, 2017, this Court issued a civil ruling, (2017) Supreme People's Court Civil Petition No. 4548, to bring this case for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. The common agents ad litem for the retrial applicant Mediterranean Hotel and the second instance appellant Lizhen Company, and the defendants at first instance Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong, respectively Ding Jianqing and Zhang Zixiang; the common agent ad litem for the respondent SPD Bank and the third party at first instance Hou Chuxiong, Ma Hao; and the common agents ad litem for the second instance appellants Zirui Company and Sun Century Company, Jiang Guoguang and Lu Yangqi, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. During the retrial proceedings of this Court, Zirui Company and Sun Century Company applied to withdraw their retrial requests. This Court separately issued a civil ruling, (2018) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 54, permitting Zirui Company and Sun Century Company to withdraw their retrial requests. This case continues to be heard with respect to the retrial application filed by Mediterranean Hotel, and the hearing has now been concluded.

Mediterranean Hotel applied for retrial, requesting: that the original judgment be set aside; that the second item of the first instance judgment be reversed, and judgment be entered that Mediterranean Hotel shall pay SPD Bank the loan principal of RMB 120 million and interest and penalty interest totaling no more than 24% per annum within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment; and that SPD Bank bear all litigation costs of this case. Facts and grounds: 1. There is a situation in this case where the judgment exceeds the claims. SPD Bank's litigation claims did not include compound interest, yet the original judgment determined that Mediterranean Hotel should calculate compound interest on overdue interest at the penalty interest rate from December 21, 2011 (including that date), which exceeds the scope of SPD Bank's litigation claims. 2. Even setting aside the fact that the judgment exceeded the claims, there is no legal basis for applying compound interest in this case. The entrusted loan contract involved only stipulated that overdue interest during the loan term could be subject to additional penalty interest, but did not stipulate that penalty interest after the loan became overdue could be further subject to compound interest. Compound interest is only computed based on normal interest collected during the loan term. For penalty interest after April 25, 2012, compound interest should not be calculated. Moreover, the entrusted loan contract did not stipulate that SPD Bank could charge compound interest. In this case, the original judgment already imposed penalty interest at a rate of 50% above the annual interest rate of 24% for overdue loans after April 25, 2012, and further ordered that compound interest be calculated on overdue interest at the penalty interest rate from December 21, 2011 (including that date), which is clearly erroneous. 3. This case is essentially a private lending, and the method of calculating interest should be governed by the relevant provisions on private lending interest rates. The original judgment applied the relevant provisions on commercial bank loans and ruled on the basis that there is no upper limit for financial institution loan interest rates, which is an error in the application of law. The entrusted loan contract involved specified that Hou Chuxiong provided the funds, SPD Bank acted as the lender based on the borrower, purpose, amount, currency, term, and interest rate determined by Hou Chuxiong, and issued loans to Mediterranean Hotel on his behalf, supervised the use and recovery of the loans, and only charged a handling fee without bearing loan risk. According to the view expressed in the Supreme People's Court Gazette, Issue 11, 2016, in the case of "Beijing Changfu Investment Fund v. Wuhan Zhongsenhua Century Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over entrusted loan contract," the entrusted loan relationship in this case is essentially a private lending relationship between Hou Chuxiong and Mediterranean Hotel, and the method of calculating interest should be governed by the relevant provisions on private lending interest rates. (a) It is not permissible to apply the relevant provisions on financial loans merely because a financial institution acted as the trustee in this relationship; rather, the relevant legal provisions on private lending should be applied based on the substance of the conduct. (b) The original judgment should have adjudicated in accordance with the relevant provisions on private lending interest rates in effect at the time the loan was made (October 25, 2011), i.e., the highest interest rate in this case should not exceed four times the bank loan interest rate of the same type, and the portion exceeding four times should not be upheld. (c) In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases (hereinafter referred to as the Private Lending Provisions), which had already taken effect at the time of the second instance, the people's court shall not uphold any portion of overdue interest, liquidated damages, and compound interest that exceeds 24% per annum in total. Although this case cannot apply that provision, the penalty interest and interest should be adjusted based on Hou Chuxiong's actual loss in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law). In this case, with a principal of RMB 120 million, the principal and interest as of July 6, 2017 amounted to as high as RMB 807 million, with an average annual interest rate of 121%. Such a high interest rate should certainly not be upheld. 4. Even if the entrusted loan contract is determined to be a financial loan contract, its annual interest rate should still be subject to the 24% upper limit. The Supreme People's Court's Several Opinions on Further Strengthening Financial Trial Work (Fa Fa [2017] No. 22) provides: "If a borrower under a financial loan contract requests an adjustment of the portion of interest, compound interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, and other fees that totals more than 24% per annum, on the grounds that these charges are excessively high and significantly deviate from the actual loss, such a request should be upheld to effectively reduce the financing cost of the real economy." Accordingly, the loan interest rate in this case should be adjusted. 5. The original judgment omitted the fact that Hou Chuxiong collected high interest through Zeng Hansheng in the form of financing consulting service fees. On October 17, 2011, a third party, Zeng Hansheng, entered into a Financing Consulting Service Agreement with Mediterranean Hotel, stipulating that Zeng Hansheng would provide consulting services for Mediterranean Hotel's financing and facilitate Hou Chuxiong's loan of RMB 120 million to Mediterranean Hotel by way of an entrusted loan; Zeng Hansheng would charge Mediterranean Hotel a consulting service fee at the rate of 5.5% per month on the principal amount of RMB 120 million. This fact has been confirmed by the Shenzhen Arbitration Commission's Award (2015) Shenzhen Arbitration No. 1203. It can be seen that Hou Chuxiong not only utilized SPD Bank to lend funds to Mediterranean Hotel, but also obtained high returns through Zeng Hansheng's provision of financing consulting services to Mediterranean Hotel. This case has already been enforced, and this portion of the amount should also be correspondingly deducted within the scope of interest protected by law in this case.

SPD Bank argued in defense: 1. This case is a dispute over an entrusted loan contract. An entrusted loan is one of the loan business explicitly provided for in the People's Bank of China's General Rules on Loans, and belongs to financial loan contracts, not private lending. The interest rate provisions for financial loan contracts should apply the People's Bank of China's provisions on loan interest rates for financial institutions, and should not apply the interest rate provisions for private lending. Since the People's Bank of China has eliminated the upper limit on loan interest rates for financial institutions, as one of the loan businesses of financial institutions, there is no upper limit on interest rates for entrusted loans. The absence of an upper limit on financial institution loans is conducive to achieving the goal of interest rate liberalization and optimal resource allocation. Moreover, from the perspective of legislative intent, if an upper limit on interest rates were set for entrusted loans, the purpose of guiding social funds to voluntarily accept financial regulation would not be achieved. 2. The provisions in the entrusted loan contract concerning the loan interest rate, penalty interest for overdue loans, and penalty interest for overdue interest during the loan term are all legal and valid, and Mediterranean Hotel should bear the corresponding liability to SPD Bank for paying interest and for breach of contract. 3. Even if the entrusted loan contract is unclear on the calculation of compound interest or if SPD Bank did not request compound interest in its lawsuit, this cannot become a reason for Mediterranean Hotel to avoid liability for breach of contract in paying penalty interest. 4. The entrusted loan contract in this case and the Financing Consulting Service Agreement are separate legal relationships both in fact and in law, and are lawful agreements reached by the parties based on their true intent. There is no issue of Hou Chuxiong and Zeng Hansheng jointly collecting interest.

Zirui Company and Sun Century Company stated that they had already reached a settlement agreement with SPD Bank and jointly paid RMB 235 million to SPD Bank, and a separate accounting would be made after this case is adjudicated.

Lizhen Company, Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong held the same view as Mediterranean Hotel. Hou Chuxiong held the same view as SPD Bank.

SPD Bank filed the following litigation claims with the court of first instance: 1. Determine that the Entrusted Loan Contract entered into by SPD Bank, Mediterranean Hotel, and Hou Chuxiong is lawful and valid, and order Mediterranean Hotel to immediately repay SPD Bank the loan principal of RMB 120 million and the related loan interest and penalty interest (Note: the amount of overdue interest as of June 6, 2012, is RMB 16,237,208.73, and the interest after June 6, 2012, shall be calculated in accordance with the provisions of the entrusted loan contract). 2. Determine that SPD Bank has a mortgage right over the property mortgaged by Lizhen Company (the parcel of land located at No. 140204092292, Jiangnan Binfang Avenue, Meijiang District, Meizhou City), and that SPD Bank has the right to be compensated from the mortgaged property in accordance with law with priority over the loan claims in this case. After SPD Bank disposes of the mortgaged property in accordance with law, if the mortgaged property is insufficient to satisfy the loan claims of SPD Bank in this case, Lizhen Company shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the portion of claims not satisfied by SPD Bank in this case. 3. Based on the loan guarantee commitments, order Zirui Company, Sun Century Company, Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong to bear joint and several liability for compensation to SPD Bank for the loan debt of Mediterranean Hotel in this case. 4. Order Mediterranean Hotel, Lizhen Company, Zirui Company, Sun Century Company, Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong to bear all litigation costs of this case jointly and severally.

The court of first instance found the following facts after trial:

On October 18, 2011, SPD Bank, Mediterranean Hotel, and Hou Chuxiong entered into an Entrusted Loan Contract (No. 79032011280176). The contract stipulated that Hou Chuxiong entrusted SPD Bank to lend RMB 120 million (in words: one hundred and twenty million yuan) to Mediterranean Hotel, with an annual interest rate of 24% (monthly interest rate of 2%), a loan term of six months, and a loan contract maturity date of April 25, 2012; in addition, according to the provisions of the Entrusted Loan Contract, if Mediterranean Hotel failed to repay the loan principal and interest in full as agreed, penalty interest at a rate of 50% above the contract interest rate would be imposed on the overdue loan. To secure the realization of the loan claims under the above Entrusted Loan Contract, SPD Bank also entered into a Land Use Rights Mortgage Contract (Contract No.: YD7903201128017601, hereinafter referred to as the Mortgage Contract) with Lizhen Company, which expressly stipulated that Lizhen Company would provide mortgage security for the debt of Mediterranean Hotel under the Entrusted Loan Contract with the parcel of land located at No. 140204092292, Jiangnan Binfang Avenue, Meijiang District, Meizhou City [Land Certificate No.: Meizhou City State-Owned (2011) No. 0324, use area: 33,499 square meters]. On October 24, 2011, the mortgage registration procedures were completed at the Meizhou Bureau of Land and Resources [Certificate of Rights No.: Meizhou City Other Rights (2011) No. 065]. In addition to the above mortgage security, Zirui Company, Sun Century Company, Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong each issued a Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter (a total of five) to Hou Chuxiong, all expressly undertaking to provide joint and several guarantee security for the debt of Mediterranean Hotel under the Entrusted Loan Contract. Based on the above mortgage security and guarantee security, on October 25 and 26, 2011, SPD Bank disbursed the loan principal of RMB 120 million to Mediterranean Hotel in three tranches. At present, the loan has matured, but Mediterranean Hotel has failed to repay the loan principal and interest as agreed, and the guarantors have also failed to assume the corresponding guarantee liability, thus giving rise to this lawsuit.

It was also found that the interest on the loan before November 20, 2011 (including that date) had been paid off, but no principal or interest was repaid thereafter. Article 3.4.2 of the Entrusted Loan Contract stipulated monthly interest payment, with the interest payment date being the 20th of each month; Article 10.2 stipulated that if the borrower fails to pay loan interest on time during the loan term, the lender is entitled to impose penalty interest on the overdue interest; Article 10.4 stipulated that if the borrower fails to repay the loan principal and interest as agreed, the lender is entitled to impose penalty interest at a rate of 50% above the contract interest rate on the overdue loan.

On October 18, 2011, Lizhen Company (as mortgagor) and SPD Bank (as mortgagee) entered into the Mortgage Contract. Article 7, paragraph 1, item (11) stipulated: If the mortgagor is not the principal debtor under the contract, the mortgagee may dispose of the mortgaged property in accordance with law, but if the proceeds from the auction or sale of the mortgaged property are insufficient to satisfy all claims under the master contract or the value of the mortgaged property is insufficient to offset all claims under the master contract, the mortgagor undertakes to unconditionally bear joint and several liability for the unsatisfied portion of the claims. Article 3, paragraph 1 and Article 7, paragraph 5 stipulated: The mortgagor is obligated to cooperate with the mortgagee in completing the mortgage registration procedures with the land administration department after signing the contract, and the contract shall take effect after the mortgage registration procedures are completed. The Mortgage Contract bore the official seal of Lizhen Company and was signed by its legal representative, Wang Hui. On October 24, 2011, both parties completed the mortgage registration at the Meizhou Bureau of Land and Resources. On October 26, 2011, the Meizhou Bureau of Land and Resources issued a Certificate to SPD Bank, certifying that SPD Bank was the mortgagee. Lizhen Company denied signing the Mortgage Contract and applied for forensic examination of the authenticity of the official seal of Lizhen Company affixed to the Mortgage Contract. To prove the authenticity of the Mortgage Contract, SPD Bank also submitted the Shareholders' Meeting Resolution of Lizhen Company, which mainly stated that in October 2011, Lizhen Company held a shareholders' meeting, unanimously agreed to the mortgage matter, and authorized legal representative Wang Hui to sign the relevant documents, with shareholders Wang Hui (holding 60% of shares) and Wang Song (holding 40% of shares) in attendance. The court of first instance requested Lizhen Company to verify the authenticity of the Mortgage Contract and the Shareholders' Meeting Resolution with Wang Hui and Wang Song, but Lizhen Company stated that it was unable to contact Wang Hui and Wang Song.

On October 19, 2011, Honglong Real Estate Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Honglong Company, later renamed Sun Century Company) issued a "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" to Hou Chuxiong. This commitment letter was affixed with the company seal of Honglong Company and the seal of its then legal representative (Chairman of the Board) Huang Ling. Sun Century Company denied issuing the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" and applied for a forensic examination of the authenticity of the Honglong Company seal affixed to the commitment letter. To prove the authenticity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter," SPD Bank also submitted the "Board Resolution" of Honglong Company, the main content of which was: on October 17, 2011, Honglong Company held a board meeting, presided over by Chairman Huang Ling, with attending directors including Hua Danping, LEO-JIN, and Wang Lingyun (Note of the court of first instance: there were six directors in total at that time). The convening and procedural aspects of the meeting, the qualifications of attendees, and the voting procedures complied with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Company Law) and the company's Articles of Association, and were lawful and valid. The board resolution approved the guarantee matters involved in the case and authorized the legal representative, Huang Ling, to sign the relevant documents. The court of first instance required Sun Century Company to verify the authenticity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" and the "Board Resolution" with Huang Ling, Hua Danping, LEO JIN, and Wang Lingyun. Sun Century Company stated that the company's management personnel had changed, that the above four individuals had left the company and could not be contacted.

On October 19, 2011, Zirui Company issued a "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" to Hou Chuxiong. This commitment letter was affixed with the company seal of Zirui Company and the seal of its then legal representative (Chairman of the Board) Wei Haiyan. Zirui Company denied issuing the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" and applied for a forensic examination of the authenticity of the Zirui Company seal affixed to the commitment letter. To prove the authenticity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter," SPD Bank also submitted the "Shareholders' Resolution" of Zirui Company, the main content of which was: on October 17, 2011, Zirui Company held a shareholders' meeting, presided over by Wei Haiyan, with the attending shareholder being Honglong Company (holding 90% of the shares). The convening and procedural aspects of the meeting, the qualifications of attendees, and the voting procedures complied with the Company Law and the company's Articles of Association, and were lawful and valid. The shareholders' resolution approved the guarantee matters involved in the case and authorized the legal representative, Wei Haiyan, to sign the relevant documents. The resolution was affixed with the company seal of Honglong Company and the seal of its then legal representative, Huang Ling, as well as the company seal of Zirui Company and the seal of Wei Haiyan. The court of first instance required Zirui Company to verify the authenticity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" and the "Shareholders' Resolution" with Wei Haiyan. Zirui Company stated that the company's management personnel had changed, that Wei Haiyan had left the company and could not be contacted. Honglong Company also did not confirm the company seal of Honglong Company and the seal of its then legal representative, Huang Ling, affixed to the "Shareholders' Resolution."

It was further ascertained that: Huang Hua issued a "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" to Hou Chuxiong on October 19, 2011, without specifying the applicable law. The "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letters" issued by Zirui Company, Sun Century Company, Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong to Hou Chuxiong all stipulated that recourse could be made directly against the guarantor without the need to first dispose of the collateral.

The court of first instance held that, based on the trial of this case, the issues in dispute were summarized as follows: First, the nature of the case and whether SPD Bank was a proper plaintiff; Second, the determination of the civil liability of the borrower, Mediterranean Hotel; Third, the determination of the civil liability of each guarantor. The analysis is as follows:

I. Nature of the Case and Whether SPD Bank is a Proper Plaintiff

According to Article 7, paragraph 2 of the "General Rules for Loans" ([1996] No. 2), a entrusted loan refers to a loan where funds are provided by an entrusting party, such as a government department, enterprise/institution, or individual, and the lender (i.e., the trustee) lends, supervises the use of, and assists in recovering the loan based on the loan object, purpose, amount, term, and interest rate determined by the entrusting party. The lender (trustee) only collects a handling fee and does not bear the loan risk. In this case, the three parties, Hou Chuxiong (entrusting party), SPD Bank (trustee), and Mediterranean Hotel, signed and actually performed the "Entrusted Loan Contract," constituting an entrusted loan legal relationship. This contract was the true expression of the intentions of the three parties and was lawful and valid. However, the entrusted loan legal relationship involves three parties: the entrusting party, the trustee, and the borrower. The entrusted loan relationship among the three parties consists of two specific legal relationships: the entrustment relationship between the entrusting party and the trustee, and the loan contract relationship between the trustee and the borrower. Pursuant to the "Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Determine the Subject of Litigation in Disputes over Entrusted Loan Agreements" (Fa Fu [1996] No. 6), when a dispute arises during the performance of an entrusted loan contract due to the borrower's failure to repay the loan on time, the lender (trustee) may file a lawsuit with the People's Court on the grounds of a loan contract dispute. Therefore, the nature of this case should be determined as a loan contract dispute, and SPD Bank is a proper plaintiff.

II. Determination of the Civil Liability of the Borrower, Mediterranean Hotel

Interest on the loan involved in this case before November 20, 2011 (inclusive) has been repaid, and neither the principal nor the interest thereafter has been repaid. Mediterranean Hotel did not dispute this, and the court of first instance confirmed it. Mediterranean Hotel argued in its defense that this case was a private lending arrangement, and the total amount of interest and default interest outside the loan term should be limited to four times the benchmark interest rate for comparable loans of the same term published by the People's Bank of China on the same date. However, private lending refers to loan contract disputes other than commercial bank financial lending. Although the specific content of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" was actually determined by the entrusting party and the borrower through prior negotiation, the lender in this case, SPD Bank, is a commercial bank and must comply with the relevant regulations of the national financial regulatory authorities regarding commercial bank lending business. The rules for handling private lending disputes do not apply to this case. Pursuant to Article 204 of the Contract Law, the interest rates for loans by financial institutions engaged in lending business shall be determined within the upper and lower limits of loan interest rates prescribed by the People's Bank of China. Article 3 of the "Notice of the People's Bank of China on Issues Concerning the Interest Rates of RMB Loans" (Yin Fa [2003] No. 251) stipulates: "Regarding the issue of default interest rates. The default interest rate for overdue loans (loans where the borrower fails to repay on the date agreed in the contract) shall be changed from the current daily rate of 0.21 per thousand to 30%-50% over the loan interest rate specified in the loan contract. For loans that are overdue or used for purposes not specified in the contract, interest shall be charged at the default interest rate from the date of overdue or the date of use not in accordance with the contract until the principal and interest are fully repaid. For interest that cannot be paid on time, compound interest shall be charged at the default interest rate." Article 2, paragraph 1 of the "Notice of the People's Bank of China on Adjusting the Deposit and Loan Interest Rates of Financial Institutions" (Yin Fa [2004] No. 251) stipulates: "The upper limit for loan interest rates of financial institutions (excluding urban and rural credit cooperatives) shall no longer be set. For loans of commercial banks and the commercialized management of loans by policy banks, the interest rate shall no longer be subject to upper limit management, and the downward floating range of loan interest rates remains unchanged." The "Entrusted Loan Contract" in this case was the true expression of the parties' intentions. The provisions regarding the loan interest rate, default interest on overdue amounts, and default interest on deferred interest during the loan term did not violate the above laws or the provisions of the industry regulatory authority's normative documents. They were lawful and valid. Mediterranean Hotel should bear the corresponding liability for breach of contract as agreed. The defenses of Mediterranean Hotel had no factual or legal basis and were not upheld.

III. Determination of the Civil Liability of Each Guarantor

(A) The Civil Liability of Lizhen Company. Lizhen Company denied signing the "Mortgage Contract" and applied for a forensic examination of the authenticity of the Lizhen Company seal affixed to the "Mortgage Contract." SPD Bank submitted the "Mortgage Contract" and the "Shareholders' Meeting Resolution" of Lizhen Company. The "Mortgage Contract" was not only affixed with the company seal of Lizhen Company but also signed and confirmed by its legal representative, Wang Hui. The parties had already registered the mortgage with the registration authority. Such mortgage registration could not have been completed without the assistance of Lizhen Company. The shareholders of Lizhen Company, Wang Hui (holding 60% of the shares) and Wang Song (holding 40% of the shares), attended the shareholders' meeting and agreed to the mortgage matters involved in the case and authorized the legal representative, Wang Hui, to handle the matter. Wang Hui and Wang Song are the current shareholders of Lizhen Company, and Wang Hui is the current legal representative. Lizhen Company did not prove that Wang Hui and Wang Song had any objection to the authenticity of the "Shareholders' Meeting Resolution" or the "Mortgage Contract." The above evidence corroborated each other and was sufficient to establish the authenticity of the "Mortgage Contract." There was no need for a forensic examination in this case, and the application for such an examination was denied. Pursuant to Article 187 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, the mortgage right was established upon registration. SPD Bank is entitled to priority compensation from the mortgaged property. According to the "Mortgage Contract," if the proceeds from the disposal of the mortgaged property by SPD Bank are insufficient to satisfy the claims involved in this case, Lizhen Company shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the claims not satisfied by SPD Bank.

(B) The Civil Liability of Other Parties to Guarantee Contracts. 1. Regarding the authenticity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" issued by Sun Century Company. Sun Century Company denied issuing the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" and applied for a forensic examination of the authenticity of the Honglong Company seal affixed to the commitment letter. SPD Bank submitted the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" and the "Board Resolution" issued by Honglong Company. The "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" was not only affixed with the company seal of Honglong Company but also with the seal of its then legal representative (Chairman of the Board), Huang Ling. At that time, Honglong Company had six directors, and those attending the board meeting were Huang Ling, Hua Danping, LEO JIN, and Wang Lingyun, which complied with the company's Articles of Association. The "Board Resolution" approved the guarantee matters involved in the case and authorized the legal representative, Huang Ling, to sign the relevant documents. Sun Century Company did not prove that Huang Ling, Hua Danping, LEO JIN, and Wang Lingyun had any objection to the authenticity of the "Board Resolution" or the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter." The above evidence corroborated each other and was sufficient to establish the authenticity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter." There was no need for a forensic examination in this case, and the application for such an examination was denied. 2. Regarding the authenticity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" issued by Zirui Company. Zirui Company denied issuing the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" and applied for a forensic examination of the authenticity of the Zirui Company seal affixed to the commitment letter. SPD Bank submitted the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" and the "Shareholders' Resolution" issued by Zirui Company. The "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" was not only affixed with the company seal of Zirui Company but also with the seal of its then legal representative (Chairman of the Board), Wei Haiyan. The shareholders' meeting of Zirui Company was presided over by Wei Haiyan, with the attending shareholder being Honglong Company (holding 90% of the shares). The shareholders' meeting passed a resolution approving the guarantee matters involved in the case and authorizing the legal representative, Wei Haiyan, to sign the relevant documents. The "Shareholders' Resolution" was affixed with the company seal of Honglong Company and the seal of its then legal representative, Huang Ling, as well as the company seal of Zirui Company and the seal of Wei Haiyan. Zirui Company did not prove that Wei Haiyan or Huang Ling had any objection to the authenticity of the "Shareholders' Resolution" or the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter." The above evidence corroborated each other and was sufficient to establish the authenticity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter." There was no need for a forensic examination in this case, and the application for such an examination was denied. 3. Regarding the applicable law for the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" issued by Huang Hua. Huang Hua is a resident of Hong Kong. The "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" issued by Huang Hua did not specify the applicable law. Therefore, the law with the closest connection to the guarantee contract relationship, i.e., the law of Mainland China (the People's Republic of China), shall apply to determine the validity of the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter." 4. Regarding whether SPD Bank can assert its rights based on the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letters." Zirui Company, Sun Century Company, Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong all issued the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" to Hou Chuxiong. However, the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" clearly stated the provision of joint and several guarantee liability for the loan involved in this case. The "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter" was the true expression of the intentions of each party and was lawful and valid. Therefore, the lender, SPD Bank, is entitled to require Zirui Company, Sun Century Company, Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong to bear joint and several liability for the loan involved in this case based on the "Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter." After fulfilling their liability for compensation, each guarantor may seek recourse from Mediterranean Hotel.

In conclusion, the claims of SPD Bank were established and were upheld by the court of first instance. Pursuant to Articles 198, 204, 205, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law, Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 176, 179, and 187 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 41 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, and Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment was as follows: 1. The "Entrusted Loan Contract" signed by SPD Bank, Mediterranean Hotel, and Hou Chuxiong was confirmed to be lawful and valid; 2. Mediterranean Hotel shall, within fifteen days from the date this judgment takes effect, pay to SPD Bank the loan principal of RMB 120,000,000 (RMB 120 million) plus interest and default interest [Interest before November 20, 2011 (inclusive) has been repaid; during the loan term, i.e., from November 21, 2011, to April 25, 2012 (inclusive), interest shall be calculated at the loan interest rate of 24% per annum; thereafter, default interest shall be calculated at 50% above the loan interest rate. The "Entrusted Loan Contract" stipulates interest payment on the 20th of each month. Compound interest shall be calculated on deferred interest from December 21, 2011 (inclusive) at the aforementioned default interest rate]; 3. SPD Bank is entitled to priority compensation from the mortgaged property involved in this case within the scope of the claims in the aforementioned second item [i.e., the land use right of Lot No. 140204092292, located at Jiangnan Bin Fang Avenue, Meijiang District, Meizhou City, Guangdong Province, under the name of Lizhen Company, Certificate No.: Meizhou National Use (2011) No. 0324, area: 33,499 square meters]. If, after lawful disposal of the mortgaged property, the mortgaged property is insufficient to satisfy the debt of Mediterranean Hotel in the second item, Lizhen Company shall bear joint and several liability for the unsatisfied portion of the debt. Lizhen Company, after assuming the guarantee liability, is entitled to seek recourse from Mediterranean Hotel; 4. Zirui Company, Sun Century Company, Huang Hua, Wang Hui, and Li Qiong shall bear joint and several liability for the debt of Mediterranean Hotel in the aforementioned second item. After fulfilling their liability, they are entitled to seek recourse from Mediterranean Hotel. The court acceptance fee for this case was RMB 722,986.04, and the property preservation fee was RMB 5,000, both to be borne by Mediterranean Hotel, with the other defendants in this case bearing joint and several liability.

Mediterranean Hotel appealed, requesting the revocation of the part of the second item of the first-instance judgment concerning interest and default interest; and a change in the calculation method of interest and default interest in this case to no more than the benchmark interest rate of the People's Bank of China for loans of the same term and type. Facts and Reasons: 1. The first-instance judgment found the facts incorrectly. (a) The substance of the entrusted loan is private lending, and the financial institution is merely the trustee of the entrusting party. According to Article 402 of the Contract Law, the creditor under the entrusted loan contract in this case is Hou Chuxiong, and the debtor is Mediterranean Hotel. The essence of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" is that Hou Chuxiong lent money to Mediterranean Hotel, i.e., a private lending contract. According to Article 7, paragraph 2 of the "General Rules for Loans," entrusted loans are essentially intermediary business of banks, where the entrusting party is the creditor and the borrower is the debtor. SPD Bank acts only as an agent for Hou Chuxiong in the entrusted loan relationship. Article 4 of the "Administrative Measures for Entrusted Loans of Commercial Banks" (Draft for Comments) also stipulates that the entrusted loan business is a entrustment agency business of commercial banks. (b) Entrusted loans are independent of loans managed on a commercial basis by financial institutions, and the state strictly limits their interest rates. Article 5 of the 1996 "Announcement of the People's Bank of China on Strictly Enforcing Financial Discipline and Prohibiting Illegal Increases in Interest Rates" stipulates that "the interest rate for entrusted loans shall be negotiated between the entrusting parties, but the maximum limit shall not exceed the interest rate for loans of the same term and type." Article 7, paragraph 2 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Disputes over Deposit Certificates" stipulates that "if the agreed interest rate in an entrusted loan exceeds the limit prescribed by the People's Bank of China, the excess portion shall be invalid." The first-instance judgment incorrectly determined the lending relationship in this case as a commercial financial lending relationship managed on a commercial basis by a commercial bank. The essence of this case is private lending, and its interest rate is strictly controlled by the state. (c) The first-instance judgment's finding regarding the amount of interest paid by Mediterranean Hotel to SPD Bank was inconsistent with the facts. The first-instance judgment incorrectly found that neither principal nor interest on the loan involved had been repaid after November 20, 2011. Within the evidence submission period at first instance, Mediterranean Hotel submitted nine "Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Loan Deduction Receipts," including the repayment of interest of RMB 2,119,333.33 before November 20, 2011 (inclusive), and the repayment of interest of RMB 2,433,081.06 after November 20, 2011. 2. The first-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly. The essence of the entrusted loan contract in this case is a private lending contract. The first-instance judgment erred in applying the relevant regulations for commercial banks. (a) The first-instance judgment inappropriately applied the "Notice of the People's Bank of China on Issues Concerning the Interest Rates of RMB Loans" and incorrectly held that the default interest rate for overdue loans could be 30%-50% higher than the loan interest rate specified in the loan contract and that compound interest could be charged at the default interest rate. The scope of application of this regulation is limited to cases where a financial institution uses its own funds to issue loans. (b) The first-instance judgment inappropriately applied the "Notice of the People's Bank of China on Adjusting the Deposit and Loan Interest Rates of Financial Institutions" and incorrectly held that the interest rate for entrusted loans, like the self-operated loan interest rates of financial institutions, has no upper limit.

Lizhen Company appealed, requesting the revocation of the third item of the first-instance judgment and the dismissal of the relevant claims filed by SPD Bank against Lizhen Company. Facts and Reasons: Lizhen Company did not sign the "Mortgage Contract." The first-instance judgment found the facts incorrectly. The first-instance judgment determined that the "Mortgage Contract" was authentic without conducting a forensic examination of the seal on the "Mortgage Contract" and the shareholders' signatures and seals on the "Shareholders' Meeting Resolution." This determination lacked a basis.

Purple Jade Company appealed, requesting that the fourth judgment item of the first-instance judgment be amended to hold that Purple Jade Company need not bear joint and several liability for the debts of Mediterranean Hotel. Facts and grounds: The findings of fact in the first-instance judgment were erroneous. During the first-instance trial, Purple Jade Company explicitly stated that it had not issued the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter in question and did not confirm the authenticity of its company seal, requesting a forensic examination of the seal. However, the first-instance court, based on the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter submitted by SPD Bank, bearing the company seal of Purple Jade Company and the seal of its then legal representative (chairman of the board) Wei Haiyan, as well as the Shareholders' Resolution attended only by Honglong Company, determined the authenticity of the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter and improperly denied Purple Jade Company's application for a forensic examination. 1. Upon reviewing the company's historical archives and records of seal usage, Purple Jade Company found no documents or records showing that it had ever signed or issued the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. 2. According to the business registration records of Mediterranean Hotel, Huang Ling, who was then the legal representative (chairman of the board) of Honglong Company, was also a shareholder of Mediterranean Hotel, holding 40% of its equity. Huang Ling, by taking advantage of her position as the then legal representative (chairman of the board) of Honglong Company, agreed to the guarantee in the name of Honglong Company. Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Company Law, where a company provides a guarantee for its shareholders or actual controller, the matter must be resolved by the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders. The shareholders referred to in the preceding paragraph, or shareholders controlled by the actual controller as referred to in the preceding paragraph, shall not participate in the voting on the matters specified in the preceding paragraph. Such voting shall be passed by more than half of the voting rights held by the other shareholders present at the meeting. Therefore, the Shareholders' Resolution of Purple Jade Company in question clearly violated the law and was legally invalid. 3. Huang Ling signed the Entrusted Loan Contract in question as the "principal responsible person/authorized representative" of the borrower, while also signing the Shareholders' Resolution of Purple Jade Company in her capacity as the legal representative of Honglong Company. Under these circumstances, SPD Bank should have known that the Shareholders' Resolution was invalid and that the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter, which was approved and authorized by that document for the legal representative of Purple Jade Company to sign, was issued in excess of authority. Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Contract Law, where a contract is made by a legal representative or responsible person of a legal person or other organization exceeding their authority, the act of representation is effective unless the counterparty knew or should have known of the excess of authority. Therefore, where SPD Bank should have known of such excess of authority, the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter issued by Wei Haiyan in the name of Purple Jade Company without authorization is invalid, and Purple Jade Company should not bear the joint and several liability for the guarantee in question. 4. The Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter issued by Wei Haiyan in the name of Purple Jade Company without authorization was also only addressed to Hou Chuxiong. Article 7.2 of the Entrusted Loan Contract provides: "The guarantee contract shall become effective upon signature by the three parties: the principal, the lender, and the guarantor." Therefore, the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter made by Wei Haiyan in the name of Purple Jade Company has no legal effect on SPD Bank. SPD Bank's claim that Purple Jade Company bear joint and several liability towards it lacks factual and legal basis.

Sun Century Company appealed, requesting that the fourth judgment item of the first-instance judgment be amended to hold that Sun Century Company need not bear joint and several liability for the debts of Mediterranean Hotel. Facts and grounds: The findings of fact in the first-instance judgment were erroneous. During the first-instance trial, Sun Century Company explicitly stated that it had not issued the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter in question and did not confirm the authenticity of its company seal, requesting a forensic examination of the seal. However, the first-instance court, based on the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter submitted by SPD Bank, bearing the company seal of Sun Century Company and the seal of its then legal representative (chairman of the board) Huang Ling, as well as the Board of Directors' Resolution presided over by Huang Ling and attended by directors Huang Ling, Hua Danping, LEO JIN, and Wang Lingyun, determined the authenticity of the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter and improperly denied Sun Century Company's application for a forensic examination. 1. Upon reviewing the company's historical archives and records of seal usage, Sun Century Company found no documents or records showing that it had ever signed or issued the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. 2. According to the business registration records of Mediterranean Hotel, Huang Ling, who was then the legal representative (chairman of the board) of Sun Century Company, was also a shareholder of Mediterranean Hotel, holding 40% of its equity. This shows that Huang Ling, as a related party, clearly took advantage of her position as the then legal representative (chairman of the board) of Sun Century Company to issue the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter in the name of Sun Century Company for the debts of her own shareholding company. Moreover, at the board meeting of Sun Century Company regarding whether to agree to the guarantee in question, Huang Ling, as a related party, was not qualified to attend and had no right to vote. Sun Century Company again applies to the court of second instance for a forensic examination of the authenticity of the company seal of Sun Century Company affixed to the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. 3. Huang Ling signed the Entrusted Loan Contract in question as the "principal responsible person/authorized representative" of the borrower, while also signing the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter and the Board of Directors' Resolution in her capacity as the legal representative of Sun Century Company. Under these circumstances, SPD Bank should have known that such documents issued by Huang Ling in the name of Sun Century Company were issued in excess of authority. Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Contract Law, where a contract is made by a legal representative or responsible person of a legal person or other organization exceeding their authority, the act of representation is effective unless the counterparty knew or should have known of the excess of authority. Therefore, where SPD Bank should have known that Huang Ling exceeded her authority, the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter issued by Huang Ling in the name of Sun Century Company without authorization is invalid, and Sun Century Company should not bear the joint and several liability for the guarantee in question. 4. The Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter issued by Huang Ling in the name of Sun Century Company without authorization was also only addressed to Hou Chuxiong. Article 7.2 of the Entrusted Loan Contract provides: "The guarantee contract shall become effective upon signature by the three parties: the principal, the lender, and the guarantor." Therefore, the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter made by Huang Ling in the name of Sun Century Company has no legal effect on SPD Bank. SPD Bank's claim that Sun Century Company bear joint and several liability towards it lacks factual and legal basis.

SPD Bank's defense against Mediterranean Hotel's grounds of appeal is as follows: First, the laws, regulations, and industry rules cited in Mediterranean Hotel's grounds of appeal are not applicable to this case. 1. The Measures for the Administration of Entrusted Loans of Commercial Banks (Draft for Comments) cited by Mediterranean Hotel has not gone through the relevant legislative procedures and is only a draft for comments. Therefore, this measure should not be used as a basis or even a reference in the trial of this case. 2. The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Cases of Disputes over Certificate of Deposit has already clarified its scope of application in Article 1. This case is a dispute over a loan contract and is not subject to these Provisions. 3. The Notice of the People's Bank of China on Strictly Observing Financial Discipline and Strictly Prohibiting Illegal Raising of Interest Rates, promulgated on February 8, 1996, was long superseded by the Notice of the People's Bank of China on Issues concerning RMB Loan Interest Rates, promulgated and implemented on December 10, 2003. That Notice explicitly states: "This Notice shall come into effect on January 1, 2004. In case of any discrepancy between the previous provisions of the People's Bank of China on RMB loan interest rates and this Notice, this Notice shall prevail." Therefore, the said Notice is not applicable to this case. Second, Mediterranean Hotel argues on appeal that the Notice of the People's Bank of China on Issues concerning RMB Loan Interest Rates and the Notice on Adjusting the Interest Rates on Deposits and Loans of Financial Institutions should not apply. The loan in this case was in the form of an entrusted loan, and the parties have no dispute on this point. According to the General Rules for Loans, an entrusted loan is a type of loan, and therefore, entrusted loans are included within the broad category of loans. The content of the two Notices is thus applicable to entrusted loans. The first-instance judgment's use of the two Notices as the trial basis for this case complies with the law and is not improper. Finally, regarding Mediterranean Hotel's assertion that it had already paid off the interest after November 20, 2011, this issue of fact shall be determined based on the bank statement of SPD Bank.

SPD Bank's defense against Li Zhen Company's grounds of appeal is as follows: Li Zhen Company claims it did not sign the Mortgage Contract, and that the first-instance court did not grant its application for forensic examination. The first-instance court's refusal to grant its application for forensic examination was in accordance with the law. A mortgage right is a type of real right and is established upon registration. After the Mortgage Contract was signed and executed, the certificate of other rights was issued with the cooperation of Li Zhen Company's personnel, and the mortgage right was established. Furthermore, the contract was signed by Wang Hui, the legal representative of Li Zhen Company. Regardless of whether the company seal affixed by Li Zhen Company on the Mortgage Contract was authentic, it cannot negate the facts recorded in the certificate of other rights and the corresponding legal consequences. The legal representative is the statutory representative of the legal person entity, and their acts represent the company. Their signature has the same effect as the company seal of Li Zhen Company. Moreover, the fact that they were authorized by a shareholders' resolution further demonstrates the authenticity and legality of their authority. That is, the signature of Wang Hui, the legal representative of Li Zhen Company, on the contract already represented the true intention of Li Zhen Company, and Li Zhen Company's cooperation in obtaining the certificate of other rights also sufficiently supports the true intention of the company.

SPD Bank's defense against the grounds of appeal of Purple Jade Company and Sun Century Company is as follows: 1. Regarding the authenticity of the company seal. The first-instance court's refusal to order a forensic examination was fully in accordance with the law, conserving judicial resources and reducing the burden of litigation. This is because, during the first-instance trial, the first-instance court required the persons who signed the relevant shareholders' resolutions and board of directors' resolutions to appear in court for questioning. Purple Jade Company and Sun Century Company failed to notify the relevant persons to appear for questioning before the first-instance court, citing an inability to contact them. Given that the relevant shareholders' resolutions and board of directors' resolutions already existed, and Purple Jade Company and Sun Century Company did not provide valid rebuttal evidence, the first-instance court determined the authenticity and legality of the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter, which complies with the law. Purple Jade Company and Sun Century Company must bear the adverse consequences of failing to provide evidence. 2. Regarding Purple Jade Company's claim that the then legal representative "Huang Ling" exceeded her authority, this has no factual or legal basis. Huang Ling signed the Entrusted Loan Contract while also signing the Shareholders' Resolution in her capacity as legal representative, which does not violate any laws or regulations. According to Article 16 of the Company Law, "Where a company provides a guarantee for its shareholders or actual controller, the matter must be resolved by the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders. The shareholders referred to in the preceding paragraph, or shareholders controlled by the actual controller as referred to in the preceding paragraph, shall not participate in the voting on the matters specified in the preceding paragraph. Such voting shall be passed by more than half of the voting rights held by the other shareholders present at the meeting." First, this article stipulates that a company shall not provide a guarantee for its shareholders or actual controller. In this case, Mediterranean Hotel is not a shareholder or actual controller of Purple Jade Company. This article is clearly not applicable to this case. Purple Jade Company's ground of appeal on this point is entirely untenable. Furthermore, the shareholders' resolution of Purple Jade Company was passed by a vote of Honglong Company, which held 90% of the shares. Huang Ling merely signed as the legal representative of Sun Century Company and did not participate in the voting. Purple Jade Company's ground of appeal is logically incoherent. As for Purple Jade Company's claim that Huang Ling took advantage of her position, this is irrelevant to this case. 3. Regarding Purple Jade Company's claim that the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter was addressed to Hou Chuxiong and its effect does not extend to the bank. First, we believe that according to Article 22 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, where a third party unilaterally issues a guarantee letter in writing to the creditor, and the creditor accepts it without raising any objection, the guarantee contract is established. The Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter was issued unilaterally by Purple Jade Company. Hou Chuxiong, the principal of the bank, accepted it. Moreover, the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter represented the true intention of Purple Jade Company and explicitly provided for joint and several liability for the loan in question. Therefore, it is certainly in accordance with the law for the bank, acting on the mandate of the creditor (Hou Chuxiong), to claim the corresponding rights against the guarantor. For similar grounds of appeal by Sun Century Company, the defense is the same as above and will not be repeated.

Huang Hua stated that he agreed with the opinions of Mediterranean Hotel and Li Zhen Company on appeal.

Wang Hui stated that he agreed with the opinions of Huang Hua and Mediterranean Hotel on appeal.

Hou Chuxiong stated that he agreed with SPD Bank's defense.

Li Qiong failed to appear in court after being properly summoned by the court.

The court of second instance confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

Additionally, the following was found: 1. During the first instance, on November 12, 2013, SPD Bank submitted to the first-instance court a "Statement on the Arrears of Interest of Meizhou Mediterranean Hotel," which stated: Interest on the loan in question before November 20, 2011 (including that day) had been paid off; after that date, neither principal nor interest on the loan had been repaid. On February 11, 2014, Mediterranean Hotel submitted to the first-instance court a "Opinion on Evidence," which stated: No objection was raised to the interest claimed by SPD Bank during the contract period, and it was confirmed. 2. On April 13, 2016, Mediterranean Hotel submitted to the court of second instance an "Application for Withdrawal of the Motion for Evidence Collection," and expressed willingness to bear the loan amount of RMB 120 million and the lawful interest not exceeding four times the bank interest rate for the same period.

The court of second instance holds that this case is a dispute over a Hong Kong-related loan contract. The parties to this case have no objection to the application of the laws of mainland China to resolve the dispute, and the court confirms this.

Based on the arguments of both parties on appeal, the issues in dispute in the second instance of this case are: 1. The calculation of interest on the loan in question; 2. Whether Li Zhen Company signed the Mortgage Contract in question and whether it should bear liability for repayment; 3. Whether Sun Century Company and Purple Jade Company issued the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter in question and whether they should bear joint and several liability.

Regarding the calculation of interest on the loan in question. According to Article 7 of the General Rules for Loans, "Entrusted loans refer to loans where funds are provided by principals such as government departments, enterprises, institutions, or individuals, and the lender (i.e., the trustee) issues, supervises the use of, and assists in the recovery of the loans on behalf of the principal in accordance with the loan objects, purposes, amounts, terms, interest rates, etc. determined by the principal. The lender (trustee) only collects a handling fee and does not bear the loan risk." In this case, the three parties, Hou Chuxiong (principal), SPD Bank (trustee), and Mediterranean Hotel (borrower), signed and actually performed the Entrusted Loan Contract in question. The three parties established an entrusted loan legal relationship. The Entrusted Loan Contract in question represented the true intention of the parties and its content does not violate the provisions of Chinese laws and regulations. The contract is legally valid. In this case, the lender SPD Bank is a commercial bank and must comply with the relevant provisions of the national financial regulatory authorities on the loan business of commercial banks. Mediterranean Hotel's appeal that the Entrusted Loan Contract in question is actually a private loan is inconsistent with the facts of this case and is not supported. Pursuant to the provisions of the Notice of the People's Bank of China on Adjusting the Interest Rates on Deposits and Loans of Financial Institutions (Yin Fa [2004] No. 251), the floating range of loan interest rates of financial institutions was relaxed, and "the upper limit for loan interest rates of financial institutions (except urban and rural credit cooperatives) is no longer set. For commercial bank loans and policy bank loans managed on a commercial basis, the upper limit for interest rates is no longer managed, and the scope for downward adjustment of loan interest rates remains unchanged." The first-instance judgment, based on the provisions of Article 3 of the Notice of the People's Bank of China on Issues concerning RMB Loan Interest Rates (Yin Fa [2003] No. 251) concerning penalty interest rates and the calculation of compound interest, and the provisions of (Yin Fa [2004] No. 251), determined that the provisions in the Entrusted Loan Contract in question regarding the loan interest rate, penalty interest for overdue repayment, and penalty interest for overdue payment of interest during the loan period did not violate the provisions of the above laws and regulatory documents of the competent authorities, were legally valid, and ordered Mediterranean Hotel to repay the loan interest to SPD Bank in accordance with the contract and bear the corresponding liability for breach of contract. This was not improper. Mediterranean Hotel's appeal that the loan interest and penalty interest agreed upon in the loan contract in question violate laws and regulations is untenable and is not supported. As for the issue of whether Mediterranean Hotel has already paid off the interest to SPD Bank. Upon examination, during the first instance, on November 12, 2013, SPD Bank submitted to the first-instance court a "Statement on the Arrears of Interest of Meizhou Mediterranean Hotel," which stated: Interest on the loan in question before November 20, 2011 (including that day) had been paid off; after that date, neither principal nor interest on the loan had been repaid. On February 11, 2014, Mediterranean Hotel submitted to the first-instance court a "Opinion on Evidence," which stated: No objection was raised to the interest claimed by SPD Bank during the contract period, and it was confirmed. Based on this, the first-instance judgment determined that interest on the loan in question before November 20, 2011 (including that day) had been paid off, and after that date, neither principal nor interest on the loan had been repaid. This determination was not improper and should be upheld.

Regarding whether Li Zhen Company signed the Mortgage Contract in question and whether it should bear liability for repayment. Upon examination, during the first instance, SPD Bank submitted the Mortgage Contract in question and the Shareholders' Meeting Resolution. The Mortgage Contract was affixed with the company seal of Li Zhen Company and signed by its legal representative Wang Hui for confirmation, and the parties had completed the mortgage registration. The Shareholders' Meeting Resolution indicated that shareholders Wang Hui (holding 60%) and Wang Song (holding 40%) of Li Zhen Company agreed to the mortgage matter and authorized legal representative Wang Hui to handle it. Li Zhen Company did not provide evidence to show that Wang Hui or Wang Song had any objections to the authenticity of the Mortgage Contract or the Shareholders' Meeting Resolution. The above evidence corroborates each other and is sufficient to establish the authenticity of the Mortgage Contract. The first-instance court's refusal to grant Li Zhen Company's application for forensic examination was not improper. Li Zhen Company's appeal that it did not sign the Mortgage Contract in question lacks basis and is not supported. The first-instance judgment, based on the provisions of the Mortgage Contract, determined that if the proceeds from the disposal of the mortgaged property are insufficient to satisfy the claim in question, Li Zhen Company shall bear joint and several liability for the portion of the claim not satisfied by SPD Bank. This determination was not improper and should be upheld.

Regarding the issue of whether Sun Century Company and Zirui Company issued the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter and should bear joint and several liability. First, Sun Century Company appealed denying that it issued the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. SPDB submitted the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter and the Board Resolution at first instance. Upon investigation, the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter bore the company seal of Honglong Company and the seal of its legal representative (chairman) at the time, Huang Ling. The Board Resolution approved the guarantee matter involved in the case and authorized the legal representative Huang Ling to sign relevant documents. Sun Century Company did not provide evidence to prove that Huang Ling, Hua Danping, LEOJIN, or Wang Lingyun had any objection to the authenticity of the Board Resolution and the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. The above evidence corroborated each other, sufficient to confirm the authenticity of the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. The first-instance judgment's decision not to grant Sun Century Company's application for forensic examination was not inappropriate. Second, Zirui Company appealed denying that it issued the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. SPDB submitted the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter and the Shareholders' Resolution at first instance. Upon investigation, the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter bore the company seal of Zirui Company and the seal of its legal representative (chairman) at the time, Wei Haiyan. The Shareholders' Resolution bore the seal of Honglong Company (holding 90% shares) and the seal of its legal representative Huang Ling, as well as the seal of Zirui Company and the seal of Wei Haiyan. Zirui Company did not provide evidence to prove that Wei Haiyan or Huang Ling had any objection to the authenticity of the Shareholders' Resolution and the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. The above evidence corroborated each other, sufficient to confirm the authenticity of the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter. The first-instance judgment's decision not to grant Zirui Company's application for forensic examination was not inappropriate. The aforementioned Board Resolution, Shareholders' Resolution, and Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter did not violate any prohibitive provisions of the law and were all lawful and valid. The first-instance judgment ordering Sun Century Company and Zirui Company to bear joint and several liability based on the Loan Guarantee Commitment Letter was not inappropriate and should be upheld.

In summary, the appeal requests of Mediterranean Hotel, Lizhen Company, Sun Century Company, and Zirui Company cannot be established and should be dismissed; the first-instance judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law, and should be upheld. Pursuant to subparagraph (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed. The second-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 842,209.29, of which Mediterranean Hotel shall bear RMB 119,223.25; Lizhen Company, Sun Century Company, and Zirui Company shall each bear RMB 240,995.35. Lizhen Company, Sun Century Company, and Zirui Company have each prepaid the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 722,986.04, and the court of second instance shall refund RMB 481,990.69 to each of Lizhen Company, Sun Century Company, and Zirui Company.

Upon retrial, this court finds that the authorized litigation representative of SPDB stated at the first-instance trial (page 6 of the trial transcript): "The overdue interest shall accrue from December 21, 2011."

In addition, it is further found that on July 6, 2017, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court issued the Enforcement Ruling (2017) Yue 03 Zhi No. 2000. The ruling recorded that to enforce the original judgment in this case, the property of Mediterranean Hotel and others (limited to RMB 807,133,353 and interest, etc.) was sealed, frozen, or garnished.

Other facts found in this retrial are consistent with those found in the original trial.

This court is of the opinion that, synthesizing the opinions of all parties, the issues in dispute in this retrial are: 1. Whether there is a situation of adjudicating beyond the scope of the claims; 2. How the interest on the loan involved in the case should be determined.

I. Regarding whether there is a situation of adjudicating beyond the scope of the claims

Mediterranean Hotel argues that SPDB's claims did not include the payment of compound interest, but the original judgment found that Mediterranean Hotel should, from December 21, 2011 (including that day), calculate compound interest on deferred interest at the penalty interest rate, thus exceeding the scope of SPDB's claims. This court is of the opinion that Article 10.2 of the Entrusted Loan Contract in this case stipulates: If the borrower fails to pay loan interest on time during the loan period, the lender has the right to charge a penalty on the deferred interest; Article 10.4 stipulates: If the borrower fails to repay the loan principal and interest as agreed, the lender has the right to charge a penalty of 50% above the contract interest rate on the overdue loan. It can be seen that Article 10.2 and Article 10.4 of the Entrusted Loan Contract actually respectively stipulate the "penalty for deferred interest" (i.e., compound interest) and the "penalty for overdue loan" (i.e., penalty interest in the general sense). Although SPDB's relevant claim was generally expressed as: "Mediterranean Hotel shall immediately repay SPDB the loan principal of RMB 120 million and the relevant loan interest and penalty interest (Note: the amount of overdue interest as of June 6, 2012, is RMB 16,237,208.73; interest after June 6, 2012, shall be calculated according to the terms of the Entrusted Loan Contract)", with respect to the claim for interest after June 6, 2012, to be calculated according to the Entrusted Loan Contract, the penalty interest claimed did not exceed the scope of Articles 10.2 and 10.4 of the Entrusted Loan Contract. Furthermore, the contract in this case stipulated that the interest payment date was the 20th of each month, and both parties acknowledged that the interest before November 20, 2011, had been repaid. According to Article 10.2, the interest payable on December 20, 2011, but not paid, shall accrue "penalty for deferred interest" i.e., compound interest, from the following day. The statement by SPDB's authorized litigation representative at the first-instance trial that "overdue interest shall accrue from December 21, 2011" is also consistent with the agreement on compound interest in Article 10.2. In summary, the original judgment's interpretation of the penalty interest in SPDB's claim as "penalty for overdue loan" and "penalty for deferred interest" and its ruling accordingly did not constitute adjudicating beyond the scope of SPDB's claims. Mediterranean Hotel's argument that there was a situation of adjudicating beyond the claims lacks basis, and this court does not support it.

II. Regarding how the loan interest in the case should be determined

According to Article 7 of the General Rules for Loans, an entrusted loan refers to a loan where the entrusting party (government departments, enterprises, institutions, individuals, etc.) provides the funds, and the lender (i.e., the trustee) grants, monitors use, and assists in recovering the loan in accordance with the loan object, purpose, amount, term, interest rate, etc., determined by the entrusting party. The lender (trustee) only charges a handling fee and bears no loan risk. At the same time, relevant regulations of the People's Bank of China also clarify that entrusted loans are an intermediate business of commercial banks, constituting neither on-balance-sheet assets nor on-balance-sheet liabilities, and only generate non-interest income for banks. It can be seen that entrusted loans have been brought under national financial supervision. In this legal relationship, the lender is a lending institution approved by national financial regulatory authorities to engage in lending business, and it should fulfill the duties of granting, monitoring use, and assisting in loan recovery on behalf of the entrusting party, which is similar to financial loan contracts. However, on the other hand, entrusted loans also have similarities with private lending. First, although the financial institution is the lender, it actually acts as a trustee in entering into the loan relationship with the borrower, rather than independently deciding on the loan; the determination of the main rights and obligations in the loan contract, such as the loan object, purpose, amount, term, and interest rate, still reflects the will of the entrusting party. Second, from the perspective of actual bearing of rights and obligations, it is the entrusting party, not the lender, that enjoys the main contractual rights such as loan interest income and actually bears the risk of the borrower's default or late payment. Third, unlike proprietary loans of financial institutions where funds are raised through statutory channels, entrusted loans directly come from the entrusting party's own funds, which is no different from a lender using its own funds for private lending. It can be seen that entrusted loans exhibit characteristics of both financial loans and private lending in different aspects. Where current laws and judicial interpretations do not explicitly regulate entrusted loans, the applicable rules can be determined by analyzing whether the relevant issue is more characteristic of financial loans or private lending. Current laws and judicial interpretations do not impose a cap on the interest rate ceiling for entrusted loans. Given that it is the entrusting party, not the lending financial institution, that determines the main contract terms such as the interest rate and actually receives the interest, and considering that entrusted loans and private lending share the same source of funds, their capital costs can be presumed to be roughly equivalent.
